articles.title: Veerle Buurman scrambles late WCL winner to push blunt Chelsea past PSG
articles.summary: Chelsea were made to work hard for three Champions League points against a resilient Paris Saint-Germain side but their patience paid off, Veerle Buurman squeezing the ball in at the near post to put them, temporarily at least, at the top of the table in the league phase.
body: Buurman had stolen the show in Chelsea’s defeat of Manchester City at the weekend, coming on 12 minutes in and nullifying Khadija Shaw’s threat to be named player of the match and she was the hero under the lights with Chelsea doing everything but score prior to her goal.

Sonia Bompastor’s side had been frustrated by Häcken last week, held to a 0-0 draw by the Swedish side and falling out of the top four automatic progression places. There was a desire to put things right at AFC Wimbledon’s stadium and they did just that, albeit in not the prettiest of encounters.

PSG had suffered a 2-1 home defeat to Bayern Munich after three draws and one win in the competition ahead of their trip to London. Denied a point late on, they remain 10th and dangerously close to slipping out of a place in the playoffs.

Chelsea had been thrillingly gutsy and diligent in their 1-0 win over Manchester City on Saturday and against PSG they were similarly solid at the back, but they lacked spark in attack. Ellie Carpenter became the focal point of their forward play from the right, with the striker Melvine Malard injured in the game against City.

articles.title: MLB commissioner Manfred cites fan support for salary cap as baseball heads towards lockout
articles.summary: 2027 season under threat amid dispute over salary cap. Commissioner says fans want a more equal game. MLB commissioner, Rob Manfred, has insisted owners will not budge from their demand for a salary cap, leaving the league on track for a lockout starting 2 December that could threaten the 2027…
body: “I can’t imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor,” Manfred said on Wednesday at a news conference during an owners meeting. Players say they will never accept a cap. The last time management proposed a cap in 1994, it led to a strike that lasted almost eight months and caused the cancellation of the World Series for the first time in 90 years.

“There’s plenty of room for compromise, but there’s one thing that I will not compromise and that’s the issue that we’re hearing from the vast majority of our fans: They want a salary cap and floor and on that we will not compromise,” Manfred continued. “We are not prepared to tell 70% of our fans that they’re wrong on this issue. Competitive balance is a serious problem, and it needs to be addressed and it’s one that we can’t avoid just because the negotiation may be difficult.”

Baseball’s five-year collective bargaining agreement expires at 11.59pm EST on 1 December. A lockout, which would be the sport’s 10th work stoppage since 1972, would bring to a halt all trades and signings.

articles.title: Rugby brain injury lawsuits again on brink of collapse over medical documents delay
articles.summary: Claimants’ legal team argues for extension until January. Future of case rests on decisions of the two judges. After six years of interminable and expensive legal argument, the two lawsuits involving hundreds of brain-damaged rugby players appear to be on the brink of collapsing.
body: The lead counsel representing the players, Paul Downes KC, had conceded in June that the claimants were in the “last-chance saloon” after repeatedly missing court-mandated deadlines for the disclosure of documents to the defendants. Having done so again this October, they now appear to be somewhere out beyond it.

As the legal team representing World Rugby, the Rugby Football Union and the Welsh Rugby Union have argued, “there is no watering hole” in sight. The latest set of court hearings were supposed to mark a watershed in the case’s progression towards a trial beginning next October.

The sides were due to submit their shortlists of potential test cases to stand trial, but the defendants have argued that they are unable to complete the process because they still have not received the necessary medical documents from the claimants’ legal team, despite a series of court orders obliging the claimants to disclose them.

articles.title: ‘An honour’: Pochettino up for challenge of leading Manchester United revival
articles.summary: New head coach faces tough opening match at Anfield. ‘It’s a big challenge but at the same time it’s adrenaline’ Mauricio Pochettino said it was “an honour” and “a privilege” to be the new Manchester United head coach after arriving in England on Wednesday.
body: Pochettino flew from Cincinnati to Manchester overnight after overseeing the USA beating Haiti in his final game in charge. Members of Pochettino’s staff landed earlier in the week to begin work at Carrington, laying the foundations as United seek to turn their season around. His right-hand man, Jesús Pérez, the goalkeeping coach Toni Jiménez and the fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino, who continues to work with his father, have already taken training with those not on international duty.

Those away with their national teams will return to the club on Thursday, when they are expected to meet Pochettino for the first time and hold meetings. Conversations have also been held with various departments within the club, as Pochettino sought to learn about the squad’s health as he seeks areas of improvement.

articles.title: Chelsea snatch late winner vs PSG to move top of WCL table
articles.summary: Veerle Buurman's late winner snatched a late 1-0 win for Chelsea against Paris Saint-Germain to move them to the top of the Champions League table.
body: Sonia Bompastor's side looked as if they were heading to back-to-back goalless draws, following the 0-0 draw with BK Hacken last time out in Europe, until Buurman was able to bundle her effort home at the near post in the 88th minute.
The hosts had been the dominant side throughout but were thwarted by Katarzyna Kiedrzynek on more than one occasion.
Alyssa Thompson had come close to breaking the deadlock just before the break after seeing her initial shot and follow-up effort smothered by Kiedrzynek.
The corner for Buurman's timely winner arrived after the PSG goalkeeper got down well to her right to keep Sjoeke Nusken's header out.

articles.title: Littler stunned by Wattimena at Grand Slam of Darts
articles.summary: Luke Littler's title defence at the Grand Slam of Darts is over after he suffered a 10-8 loss to Jermaine Wattimena in the last 16 in Wolverhampton.
body: It was simply a stunning performance from Wattimena in which he averaged 101.7, outscoring the world No 1 and outplaying him in every facet, hitting 10 180s and 11 140s on the way.
The loss for Littler means that he will not join Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen on a short but illustrious list of players who have won the Grand Slam three times in a row.

Littler had picked up the Grand Slam title in 2024 with a win over Martin Lukeman and then backed that up with victory over Luke Humphries in 2025. But his attempt at a hat-trick was shattered with Wattimena's win blowing the competition wide open.
"It feels emotional, absolutely incredible," Wattimena told Sky Sports immediately after the victory.

articles.title: Ukrainian FA to blame for failed drugs test - Mudryk
articles.summary: Tottenham's on-loan Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk says he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban.
body: The 25-year-old, on a season-long loan from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium, which he believes entered his system while on international duty.
Having initially faced a four-year ban from the Football Association (FA), his appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport was successful.
He returned to football after accepting he had breached anti-doping rules and agreeing to a suspension equivalent to the time he had already served.
After appearing for Chelsea during a pre-season tour of Asia, Mudryk joined Tottenham on transfer deadline day to reunite with his former Shakhtar Donetsk manager Roberto de Zerbi.

articles.title: FA explored legal challenge to Infantino staying on
articles.summary: The Football Association considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, but it felt a case was likely to fail.
body: The Football Association has considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, BBC Sport can reveal.
But it believes any attempt to prevent him from standing in the election in March is likely to fail.
Infantino oversaw the introduction of a three-term limit when he replaced Sepp Blatter as leader of world football's governing body.
However, Fifa's council agreed in 2022 that his first period in office from 2016 to 2019 should not count as it was the remainder of his predecessor's interrupted final term.

articles.title: Cadillac confirm Bottas to stay with team for 2027
articles.summary: Cadillac have confirmed Valtteri Bottas will stay on at the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season, ending speculation about the Finnish driver's future.
body: Bottas returned after a year's absence from the grid for this season, Cadillac's first in the sport, as one of two hugely experienced drivers for the all-new American team's first line-up alongside Sergio Perez, who signed a contract extension last month until at least 2029.

But, Bottas' future has been up in the air recently as Cadillac pushed for American Formula 2 driver Colton Herta to earn a Formula 1 super licence, which he secured two weeks ago, by running him in practice sessions.
The team have committed to Bottas for another year though, citing the 37-year-old's "extensive Formula 1 experience, technical insight and race-winning pedigree to the team".
"To whom it may concern, I'm staying!" said Bottas, in reference to his team radio after winning the 2019 Australian Grand Prix with Mercedes.

articles.title: Hemp stars as Man City beat Hacken in Champions League
articles.summary: Lauren Hemp scored one and assisted another as Manchester City beat BK Hacken 2-0 in their penultimate Women's Champions League league phase game on Wednesday.
body: After a goalless first half in which the WSL champions struggled to break down a stubborn Hacken, Andree Jeglertz played his aces at half-time, bringing on Hemp and Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw.

The England international immediately brought a spark and directness Man City had been lacking in the first 45 minutes. Aoba Fujino was their best attacking threat to that point, but was one of the players - along with Beth Mead, who was largely ineffective - who made way at the break.

It was a fortuitous opener for Hemp, although made by her own tenacity. She wriggled through two defenders into the box, with Emma Ostlund's clearance hitting her on the shin before beating Jennifer Falk.
She hit the post too not long after as Man City looked for the comfort of a second, and soon found it as Hemp and Shaw linked up perfectly.

articles.title: Barcelona sporting director Deco regrets failing to sign Luis Díaz
articles.summary: Last year, Bayern Munich shelled out €70million for the services of Luis Díaz who arrived from Premier League giants Liverpool. In signing the Colombian, the German record champions prevailed over FC Barcelona, much to the annoyance of the Catalan club.
body: This was indirectly confirmed by Deco, sporting director of the reigning La Liga title holders, on the program 'Tot Costa' on Catalunya Ràdio.
When asked which player he would have liked to sign but didn't manage to, the Portuguese legend simply replied: “Luis Díaz”.
At the time of the transfer, Barça was in a very precarious financial situation and therefore unable to pay the transfer fee.
Díaz has since performed strongly in a Bayern Munich shirt. In 62 games, the winger has scored 31 goals and provided 24 assists.

articles.title: Fantasy football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em WR in Week 11: Fire up Josh Downs with confidence vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Jaylen Waddle is on track to face a vulnerable Raiders secondary following his concussion, while Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant remain viable options in deeper formats
body: Jaylen Waddle (concussion) practiced Wednesday, and he appears set to play in Week 11 against Las Vegas. He left Week 9 at Carolina with a concussion and then Denver was on bye in Week 10, but Waddle should be considered a No. 2 Fantasy receiver in all leagues against the Raiders.

Las Vegas is No. 9 in most Fantasy points allowed to opposing receivers, and 15 receivers have scored at least 10.4 PPR points against the Raiders this season. Waddle scored 14.9 PPR points in his last healthy game in Week 8 against Kansas City with three catches for 39 yards and a touchdown on six targets, along with a two-point conversion, and we were hoping that was the start of a quality finish for Waddle.

He should get back on track in Week 11 given the matchup, and we're glad he's healthy. Waddle's return limits the upside for Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant, but both are worth starting in three-receiver leagues.
It's time for Waddle to be a star. He had a rough start to his tenure in Denver, but he can start to deliver in a big way in Fantasy and reality for the Broncos to end the season.
